newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria may make French compulsory in schools.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria may make French compulsory in schools.

text.p: English-speaking Nigeria could make the study of French compulsory in schools, according to remarks by military ruler General Sani Abacha reported in local newspapers on Wednesday.
"We should consider seriously the possibility of making French language compulsory in schools," Abacha said on Tuesday in the capital Abuja when he received the report of a panel on higher education.
Nigeria, the leading regional power, is surrounded by French-speaking countries who form a majority in the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

Suspended from the Commonwealth, which groups Britain and its former colonies, over the hanging of nine minority rights activists in 1995, Nigeria has since forged closer ties with other regional blocs.
In December, Abacha made a surprise appearance at the summit of Francophone nations in Burkina Faso.
The semi-official Daily Times reported that Abacha said it was in the national interest for Nigeria to become bilingual.
"So we have to look into it within the shortest possible time, how we can, at least in our own interest, encourage people to learn to speak French," he said.
